5. Deviations from spec
- Briefed F1 spelling "git commit -m x -m -i -- <ledger>" is NOT pinned. Measured: git reads -i there as the second -m's value (a message paragraph), so no --include exists and admitting it is correct; a BLOCK pin would force a false positive onto the F slice. Pinned instead the spellings where -i is really a flag: "-m <subject> -m -m -i" (the Critic's own -m -m -i) and "--trailer --trailer -i". Added GREEN control T5F1c (ordinary second -m paragraph).
- The bare subject "x" is replaced by "chore: reconcile ledger" (GIT-01 reads the subject first; reasoned, not measured).
- F4 pins are GREEN by design (the --help behaviour exists, it had no pin), so the Goal's "RED pins" holds for F1 and F3 only. The stop condition "a pin is green" is reported here for T5F4a/b (both files) and the controls; no RED-intended pin was green.
- F3: one negative case per class would not fit the budget well; pinned two real-push, marker-free negatives (push option, refspec count) and one bundle control. The prefix, global-option and -C classes are not pinned.
- The load hook serves the guard post-images directly from the tranche path (no scratch copy), a method detail.

6. Open items
- Independent review: pending (Elephant dispatches the Critic).
- Design question for the F slice that these pins expose: the existing T38/T80/T82 marker cases (git grep, trailer with a parenthesis) are refused with the "only git [-C <path>] push is accepted ..." reason (a global-option class reason), the heredoc case with the shell-bundle reason. If the Why line is keyed by reason string, the git grep marker case loses its Why although a marker is the true cause; keying by marker presence would keep it. The F3 pins are chosen to hold under either reading (marker-free pushes carry no Why; the bundle refusal keeps it).
- The dispatch hook's 80 % notice fired at counted call 44; the remaining steps (manifest, check, commit, record) were commit-path only and fit under the cap. No closing-allowance handover was needed.
